D:/Project/stock-trading-system-reference

LOCAL SECRET SOURCE

D:/Project/research/.env

SECURITY RULES

The .env file may be used only as a runtime credential source.

Never:

- print secret values;
- include secret values in Codex responses;
- include secret values in terminal logs;
- copy .env into another file or directory;
- commit .env;
- place credentials in fixtures;
- place credentials in state.json;
- place credentials in response.md;
- place credentials in tests;
- place credentials in exception messages;
- place credentials in documentation.

Determine required credential VARIABLE NAMES from the legacy implementation.

If credentials are missing, report only the missing variable names.

Never report their values.

If Telegram session/authentication artifacts are created, ensure they are
excluded from Git before continuing.

Verify git ignore protection before acquisition.

OBJECTIVE

Acquire ONE genuine historical Top30 Telegram source sample and preserve it
as an immutable local research artifact.

This job is deliberately narrow.

Do NOT collect the entire three-year history yet.

Do NOT join future price data.

Do NOT perform outcome analysis.

Do NOT use current KRX master information to fill historical identities.

ACQUISITION TARGET

Select one historical Top30 report/date that is accessible through the
existing Telegram acquisition mechanism.

Prefer a date sufficiently old to represent the intended historical study
and for which the original Telegram message metadata can still be retrieved.

Use only a small sample:
prefer one complete Top30 report from one historical cutoff/date.

If no genuine historical report can be acquired safely, stop and document
why rather than substituting synthetic data.

SOURCE PRESERVATION

Preserve the genuine acquired source artifact without silently rewriting
its original content.

Store an immutable/raw representation sufficient to audit:

- Telegram message ID
- channel/chat identifier in a non-secret form
- message timestamp
- edit timestamp if available
- acquisition/ingestion timestamp
- raw message content or canonical byte-preserved representation
- byte length
- SHA-256 digest
- source type
- acquisition implementation/version
- availability evidence
- provenance

Clearly distinguish:

SOURCE TIME
when Telegram says the message existed/published;

EDIT TIME
when Telegram reports a later edit, if any;

INGESTION TIME
when this research system acquired it;

AVAILABILITY CLAIM
what can actually be proven about availability at the historical cutoff.

Do not treat ingestion time as historical publication time.

Do not invent edit/deletion history that Telegram cannot provide.

AVAILABILITY SEMANTICS

Be conservative.

If the Telegram API proves the historical message timestamp but cannot prove
that the current message bytes are exactly the bytes visible at the original
cutoff, represent that limitation explicitly.

Do not automatically claim that today's retrieved message content is an
immutable historical artifact if edits may have occurred.

If an edit timestamp is after the intended cutoff, the post-edit content must
not silently become cutoff-visible historical evidence.

If historical byte-level availability cannot be proven, classify the artifact
appropriately and document the restriction.

MANIFEST

Create a deterministic manifest for the genuine source artifact using the
JOB-0007 immutable fixture mechanism where appropriate.

The manifest must bind:

- artifact ID
- Telegram source/message identity
- preserved bytes/reference
- byte length
- SHA-256
- source timestamp
- edit timestamp
- ingestion timestamp
- availability state/time
- provenance
- acquisition version

Byte modification must cause validation failure.

PARSER INTEGRATION

Run the minimum existing/new parser path needed to determine whether the
genuine artifact can produce Top30 observations.

Preserve exact source-observed stock names.

Do not require every historical stock code to resolve.

Unresolved identity is valid and preferable to retrospective guessing.

IDENTITY BOUNDARY

Use HistoricalIdentityBundle where identity evidence is genuinely available.

Current KRX/master data must not be used as point-in-time evidence.

Retrospective mappings, if useful for audit, must remain behind the
retrospective boundary.

ASSESSMENT FREEZE

Only if the acquired source satisfies the existing point-in-time contract
sufficiently for a restricted fixture experiment:

produce a write-once frozen assessment using the JOB-0007 mechanism.

If availability integrity is insufficient, do NOT force assessment creation.

Instead preserve the raw artifact/manifest and report the blocking issue.

NO OUTCOMES

This job must not access or attach:

- future OHLCV
- +5/+10/+20/+60 returns
- future sector performance
- future labels
- success/failure classifications

TESTS

Add focused tests proving at minimum:

1. .env and secret/session artifacts remain Git-ignored;
2. credential values are not persisted in generated research artifacts;
3. genuine source digest validation works;
4. byte modification fails manifest validation;
5. Telegram source/edit/ingestion timestamps remain distinct;
6. unknown edit/availability information remains explicit;
7. parser preserves source-observed stock names;
8. unresolved identities are preserved;
9. current/retrospective mapping cannot become assessment-time identity;
10. post-cutoff edit evidence cannot silently enter cutoff assessment;
11. existing JOB-0006 adversarial tests still pass;
12. existing JOB-0007 write-once tests still pass.

DATA LOCATION

Use a clear local research-data location under the target repository structure.

Do not store secrets there.

Keep the genuine source artifact small.

Do not acquire bulk history in this job.

DOCUMENTATION

Create:

docs/experiments/JOB-0008-genuine-telegram-source.md

Document:

- selected Telegram historical report/date

- provenance
- source timestamp

READINESS VERDICT

End with exactly one:

GENUINE_FIXTURE_READY
GENUINE_FIXTURE_READY_WITH_RESTRICTIONS
SOURCE_ACQUIRED_BUT_NOT_CUTOFF_VERIFIED
ACQUISITION_BLOCKED

The verdict applies only to proceeding toward one small real historical
outcome experiment.

It does NOT authorize the full three-year study.

QUALITY

Run the complete pytest suite.
Run git diff --check.

Do not commit or push.

FINAL RESPONSE

Report:

- actual model if telemetry exposes it
- whether local credentials were successfully consumed WITHOUT exposing them
- selected historical date/report
- Telegram message ID
- source/edit/ingestion timestamp status
- artifact SHA-256
- observation count

- whether assessment freeze was allowed
- tests

Never include credential values in the final response.
